MeridianRetention review, third quarter 2026

Enterprise churn halved after the April pricing change

Monthly churn among enterprise customers fell from 2.1% to 0.9% in five months. Smaller customers did not move, so the gain is real but narrow.

Only the segment that got the new pricing improved

In April we replaced per-seat pricing with usage bands for enterprise customers. Their churn fell in the first full month and has stayed down. Mid-market and small-business customers kept the old pricing, and their churn is where it was in January.

How churn is measured

Customers lost in the month, as a share of customers at the start of the month. A downgrade is not counted as a loss.

Recommendation

Extend usage bands to mid-market in the first quarter

If mid-market responds half as well as enterprise did, that retains about 40 customers a year.

The new price is worked out where usage is already measured

No new system was needed. The metering service already recorded usage for reporting; billing now reads the band from it once a month.
